parsedVerdict.reasoning: The file is a presentation-layer controller, but it holds business rules and builds persistence queries. It enforces a subscription rule: when ENABLE_FEATURE_SUBSCRIPTION is on, Basic users cannot create or update access. It also enforces ownership: an access is only changed if it belongs to the requesting user. It builds Prisma query and relation objects directly (include, orderBy, where, connect, disconnect). It also decides whether an access is PUBLIC or PRIVATE. These belong in the application, domain or infrastructure layers, not presentation. Routing, guards, request binding and turning errors into HTTP responses are fine for a presentation file.

violations.message: createAccess and updateAccess enforce a subscription rule (when ENABLE_FEATURE_SUBSCRIPTION is on, Basic users get FORBIDDEN). This business rule belongs in the application/domain layer, not presentation.

deleteAccess and updateAccess enforce an ownership check (accessService.access({ id, userId }) followed by FORBIDDEN when nothing is found). This application-level authorization rule should live in AccessService.

getAllAccesses, createAccess and updateAccess build Prisma query and relation objects (include, orderBy, where, connect, disconnect). Persistence query construction belongs in infrastructure or the service, not the controller.
The getAllAccesses map labels an access PUBLIC or PRIVATE (grantee 'Public') depending on whether it has a grantee user. This is domain/application logic placed in presentation.
